title: Cycle--clique Ramsey numbers
summary: We prove that $`R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1`$ for every pair of integers $`m\ge n\ge3`$ other than $`(m,n)=(3,3)`$, for which $`R(C_3,K_3)=6`$. This establishes the cycle–clique conjecture of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp. The proof combines expansion in a minimal counterexample with a large-clique lemma and an optimization of paths joining clique vertices. These arguments reduce the remaining cases to $`3{,}099`$ finite parameter-pattern instances, which are excluded by two exact implementations of proved inference rules. Complete programs and deduction traces accompany the paper.

review.reason: Determines cycle–clique Ramsey numbers, establishing the Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture.
